He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest Demon Deacons]] and the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]]. ==High school career== Brown attended [[Dr. Phillips High School]] in [[Dr. Phillips, Florida]] and transferred to [[The First Academy]] in [[Orlando, Florida]] for his junior year.{{cite web |last1=Welter |first1=Pat |title=Chaundee Brown ready for new beginning at Michigan |url=https://www.mynews13.com/fl/orlando/sports/2020/06/04/chaundee-brown-ready-for-new-beginning-at-michigan |website=[[News 13]] |access-date=February 27, 2021 |date=June 3, 2020}} As a senior, he averaged 24.7 points and 6.7 rebounds per game. Brown was named Florida [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] and 4A Player of the Year.{{cite web |last1=May |first1=Will |title=Spotlight: Chaundee Brown |url=https://wfuogb.com/6466/sports/spotlight-chaundee-brown/ |website=[[Old Gold & Black]] |access-date=February 27, 2021 |date=November 8, 2018}} He committed to playing college basketball for [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]] over offers from [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] and [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], among others.{{cite web |last1=Hutchinson |first1=Derick |title=How Chaundee Brown's numbers epitomize what makes this Michigan basketball team special |url=https://www.clickondetroit.com/all-about-ann-arbor/2021/02/16/how-chaundee-browns-numbers-epitomize-what-makes-this-michigan-basketball-team-special/ |website=[[WDIV-TV]] |access-date=February 27, 2021 |date=February 16, 2021}} A four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], Brown became the program's highest-ranked commitment since [[Al-Farouq Aminu]] and [[Tony Woods (basketball)|Tony Woods]] in 2008.{{cite web |last1=Zucker |first1=Joseph |title=Chaundee Brown to Wake Forest: Demon Deacons Land 4-Star SG Prospect |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2667142-chaundee-brown-to-wake-forest-demon-deacons-land-4-star-sg-prospect |website=[[Bleacher Report]] |access-date=February 27, 2021 |date=October 2, 2016}} ==College career== As a freshman, Brown was a regular starter at Wake Forest, averaging 7.6 points and three rebounds per game. In his sophomore season, he averaged 11.9 points and 4.9 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Quinn |first1=Brendan |title=With Chaundee Brown ready to play, Michigan has a new piece, a new look |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2175985/2020/11/03/chaundee-brown-michigan-wake-forest-ncaa-waiver/ |website=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=February 27, 2021 |date=November 3, 2020}} Brown averaged 12.1 points and 6.5 rebounds per game as a junior.{{cite web |last1=Sang |first1=Orion |title=Michigan basketball's Chaundee Brown wants to show why Juwan Howard wanted him this year |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2020/11/02/michigan-basketball-chaundee-brown-eligibility-juwan-howard/6131226002/ |website=[[Detroit Free Press]] |access-date=February 27, 2021 |date=November 2, 2020}} He was sidelined for eight games with ankle and calf injuries. For his senior season, Brown transferred to [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]], choosing the Wolverines over [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]] and [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]].{{cite web |last1=Hawkins |first1=James |title=Wake Forest transfer Chaundee Brown commits to Michigan |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2020/05/19/wake-forest-transfer-chaundee-brown-commits-michigan-wolverines/5221582002/ |work=[[The Detroit News]] |access-date=February 27, 2021 |date=May 19, 2020}} He received a waiver for immediate eligibility from the NCAA.{{cite web |title=Michigan's Chaundee Brown receives immediate eligibility after transfer |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/30226108/michigan-chaundee-brown-receives-immediate-eligibility-transfer |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=February 27, 2021 |date=October 30, 2020}} He averaged 8 points and 3.1 rebounds per game while shooting 41.9% from 3-point range. On April 10, 2021, Brown declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] forgoing an extra year of college eligibility.{{cite web |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2021/04/10/michigan-basketball-chaundee-brown-nba-draft/7177165002/ |title=Michigan's Chaundee Brown declares for NBA draft, says he's hiring an agent |first=Orion |last=Sang |work=[[Detroit Free Press]] |date=April 10, 2021 |access-date=April 10, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===South Bay Lakers (2021)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Brown signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on August 10, 2021.{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Chaundee Brown Jr. and Mac McClung|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-sign-chaundee-brown-jr-and-mac-mcclung-2021|website=NBA.com|date=August 10, 2021|access-date=August 14, 2021}} However, he was waived on October 15.{{cite web|title=Lakers Make Training Camp Cuts|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-make-training-camp-cuts-211015|website=NBA.com|date=October 15, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} On October 23, Brown signed with the [[South Bay Lakers]] as an affiliate player, playing one game.{{cite web|first=Nick|last=Kioski|title=South Bay Finalizes Training Camp Roster|url=https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-finalizes-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 23, 2021|access-date=October 23, 2021}} ===Los Angeles Lakers (2021)=== On November 16, 2021, Brown signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web|title=Lakers Sign Chaundee Brown Jr. to Two-Way Contract; Waive Sekou Doumbouya|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-sign-chaundee-brown-jr-to-two-way-contract-waive-sekou-doumbouya-2021|website=NBA.com|date=November 16, 2021|access-date=November 16, 2021}} However, he was waived on December 21, after making two appearances with Los Angeles.{{cite web|title=Lakers Waive Chaundee Brown Jr., Sign Mason Jones to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/lakers-waive-chaundee-brown-jr-sign-mason-jones-to-two-way-contract-2021|website=NBA.com|date=December 21, 2021|access-date=December 21, 2021}} ===Atlanta Hawks / Return to South Bay (2021–2022)=== On December 27, 2021, the [[Atlanta Hawks]] signed Brown to a 10-day contract.{{cite web|title=Hawks Sign Chaundee Brown Jr. to 10-Day Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/hawks-sign-chaundee-brown-jr-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=December 27, 2021|access-date=December 27, 2021}} After his deal expired, he returned to South Bay. On April 9, 2022, Brown signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Hawks.{{cite web|title=Hawks Sign Chaundee Brown Jr. to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-sign-chaundee-brown-jr-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=April 9, 2022|access-date=April 9, 2022}} On September 11, he was waived by the Hawks.{{Cite web |title=Hawks Request Waivers on Chaundee Brown Jr. |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-request-waivers-on-chaundee-brown-jr |access-date=September 20, 2022 |website=NBA}} ===Austin Spurs (2022–2023)=== On September 28, 2022, the [[Austin Spurs]] announced that they had acquired the returning right of Brown from [[South Bay Lakers]] for a first round pick in the 2023 NBA G League Draft and the returning player rights to [[Galen Robinson Jr.]]{{Cite web|title=Austin Spurs acquire Chaundee Brown Jr.|url=https://austin.gleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-acquire-chaundee-brown-jr|date=September 28, 2022|website=NBA.com|access-date=September 28, 2022}} On October 24, 2022, Brown joined the [[Austin Spurs]] training camp roster.{{cite web|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/austin-spurs-announce-2022-23-training-camp-roster/n-5893034|title=Austin Spurs Announce 2022-23 Training Camp Roster|website=oursportscentral.com|date=October 24, 2022|access-date=October 24, 2022}} ===Indios de Mayagüez (2023)=== On April 19, 2023, Brown signed with [[Indios de Mayagüez (basketball)|Indios de Mayagüez]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|Puerto Rican league]].{{cite tweet|number=1648780439039909897|title=#BSNPR OFICIAL: El guard/alero Chaundee Brown Jr. es el nuevo refuerzo de los Indios de Mayagüez en sustitución de Tyreke Evans.|user=LaGuerraBSN|author=La Guerra del BSN|date=April 19, 2023|access-date=April 23, 2023}} He was released on May 22 after appearing in 12 games and signed with [[Gigantes de Carolina (men's basketball)|Gigantes de Carolina]] on May 24, but left the team a day later.{{cite web|title=International and G League transactions log 2023-24: Where are former NBA players going?|url=https://hoopshype.com/lists/international-and-g-league-transactions-log-2023-24-where-are-former-nba-players-going/|website=HoopsHype.com|date=May 5, 2023|access-date=June 30, 2023}} ===Scarborough Shooting Stars (2023)=== On July 19, 2023, Brown signed with the [[Scarborough Shooting Stars]] of the [[Canadian Elite Basketball League]], making his debut two days later.{{cite web|title=Regular Season Round 18: Scarborough - Montreal 103-93|url=https://www.usbasket.com/boxScores/CEBL/2023/0721_66669_66670.asp|website=USBasket.com|date=July 21, 2023|access-date=July 22, 2023}} On July 29, he was released from the club. ===SIG Strasbourg (2023)=== On July 22, 2023, Brown signed with [[SIG Strasbourg]] of the French [[LNB Pro A]].{{cite web|title=Chaundee Brown finalise la ligne extérieure|url=https://sigstrasbourg.fr/2023/07/chaundee-brown-finalise-la-ligne-exterieure|website=SIGStrasbourg.fr|date=July 22, 2023|access-date=July 23, 2023|language=French}} On June 13, 2024, Brown was selected by the [[Valley Suns]] in the [[2024 NBA G League expansion draft]].{{cite web|title=2024-25 NBA G League Expansion Draft|url=https://gleague.nba.com/2024-expansion-draft|website=NBA.com|date=June 13, 2024|access-date=June 14, 2024}} ===New Taipei Kings (2025)=== On August 21, 2025, Brown signed with [[New Taipei Kings]] of the [[Taiwan Professional Basketball League]] (TPBL).{{cite news |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/3019411 |title=日本職籃B2得分王來了！ 尚迪加盟新北國王 |date=August 21, 2025 |work=ETtoday |access-date=August 21, 2025 }} On January 12, 2026, the [[New Taipei Kings]] terminated the contract relationship with Brown.{{cite news |url=https://sports.ettoday.net/news/3099768
